tagline: A former royal capital and World Heritage city — wander old temple ruins and cycle the island.
introHtml:
Ayutthaya was Thailand's capital for several hundred years. These days people come to walk among the old temples and stupas scattered across the city island. Some sites are just brick ruins in a field of grass; others still have a towering prang standing tall. Rent a bike or take a tram and you can spend the whole day looping past them. It's only about an hour from Bangkok, easy to reach by car or train.

Beyond the ruins, Ayutthaya is known for food that goes with the town — boat noodles, roti sai mai, and big river prawns by the water. In the late afternoon, stop by a floating market or take a boat to see the temples around the island. End the day watching the temples lit up after dark, which has its own kind of beauty.
bestTime: November–February is cool and comfortable for walking and cycling around the historic sites.

highlights.name: Ayutthaya Historical Park
highlights.blurb: The World Heritage old-town zone, with ancient temples and stupas scattered all over the city island. Cycle or ride a tram and you can see them all day.

highlights.name: Wat Mahathat (Buddha head in the tree roots)
highlights.blurb: An old temple in the middle of the island where a Buddha head is embedded in the roots of a bodhi tree — the shot everyone who comes to Ayutthaya wants to take.

highlights.name: Wat Chaiwatthanaram
highlights.blurb: A riverside temple on the Chao Phraya with a handsome row of Khmer-style prangs. It looks best in the late-afternoon golden light, and people love coming in Thai dress for photos.

highlights.name: Wat Phra Si Sanphet
highlights.blurb: Three Sri Lankan-style stupas in a row in the old royal palace grounds — the most recognizable image of Ayutthaya.

highlights.name: Ayutthaya boat noodles
highlights.blurb: The town's signature dish: small bowls with a rich broth, ordered several at a time. Several well-known shops sit around the island and near Bang Ban.

highlights.name: Roti sai mai
highlights.blurb: The famous local souvenir — a thin sheet of dough wrapped around spun sugar threads. You'll find it at just about every souvenir shop in town.

foodScene.name: Boat noodles (kuaitiao ruea)
foodScene.note: The town's signature dish — a rich, concentrated broth in small bowls, ordered several at a time. Several long-running shops sit around the city island.

foodScene.name: Grilled river prawns
foodScene.note: Many riverside restaurants serve big river prawns grilled until the heads run rich, eaten with seafood dipping sauce — a dish people make the trip for.

foodScene.name: Roti sai mai
foodScene.note: The province's signature souvenir — thin sheets of dough wrapped around colorful threads of spun sugar. You can buy it to take home at almost any shop in town.

foodScene.name: Thai palace desserts
foodScene.note: Ayutthaya still has old palace-style Thai sweets to try, including thong yip, thong yot, and foi thong, found at markets and dessert shops.

foodScene.name: Floating markets and street food
foodScene.note: Ayothaya Floating Market and the markets around town have plenty to graze on — fried snacks, sweets, and one-plate dishes at local prices.

foodScene.name: Beef noodles and braised beef
foodScene.note: Ayutthaya has several old-school beef and braised-beef noodle shops with fragrant, spiced broth — a popular lunch.

foodScene.name: Cafes on the city island
foodScene.note: Small cafes, some in old houses and some with river views, are dotted around the island — a nice place to sit with a coffee after temple-hopping.

foodScene.name: Mu kratha (Thai BBQ)
foodScene.note: A popular dinner with locals, with plenty of affordable, easygoing spots to choose from.

attractions.name: Wat Mahathat
attractions.blurb: An old temple in the middle of the island where a Buddha head sits embedded in bodhi tree roots — the photo stop everyone comes to see.

attractions.name: Wat Phra Si Sanphet
attractions.blurb: Three Sri Lankan-style stupas in a row in the old royal palace grounds — the most familiar image of Ayutthaya.

attractions.name: Wat Chaiwatthanaram
attractions.blurb: A riverside temple on the Chao Phraya with a handsome row of Khmer-style prangs. It's lovely in the late afternoon and after dark when it's lit up.

attractions.name: Wat Yai Chai Mongkhon
attractions.blurb: A big stupa you can climb for the view, with a long reclining Buddha and rows of Buddha images draped in yellow robes around the courtyard.

attractions.name: Wat Lokayasutharam (open-air reclining Buddha)
attractions.blurb: A large reclining Buddha lying out in the open among ruined stupas — a quiet corner that doesn't get crowded.

attractions.name: Wat Phutthaisawan
attractions.blurb: A riverside temple on the south side of the island, with a large prang and a well-preserved cloister, in a shady setting by the water.

attractions.name: Ayothaya Floating Market
attractions.blurb: A large floating market near the city island with food, souvenirs, and folk performances — an easygoing place to wander.

attractions.name: Boat trip around the city island
attractions.blurb: Cruise the Chao Phraya and Pa Sak rivers around the island, stopping at riverside temples and taking in waterside life in the evening.
